sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Wentzville, MO?
sections.html:
Wentzville sits in western St. Charles County, and it grew faster by percentage than any other Missouri city between 2000 and 2020, according to Wikipedia. Most homes here are owner-occupied. The city does not require an occupancy inspection when you sell, which makes the process simpler than in some nearby suburbs, but the rules change if the buyer plans to rent the house out.

The Census Bureau counted 44,372 people in 2020 and estimates 49,495 for July 1, 2025. The 2010 count was only 29,070, so the population rose about 53 percent in one decade.

sections.h2: How did Wentzville grow, and what drives its housing market?
sections.html:
Wentzville was laid out in 1855 and named for Erasmus Livingston Wentz, a chief engineer of the Northern Missouri Railroad. A post office has operated here since 1859, and the Wentzville Tobacco Company Factory was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1990. For most of its life it was a small railroad town west of the St. Louis suburbs.

General Motors is the city's major employer, through the Wentzville Assembly plant that builds full-size vans and small trucks. Wikipedia also notes that a federal contractor's processing center employed about 1,500 people here at its peak and closed in 2018, eliminating 850 jobs.

The city covers about 20 square miles and is run by a mayor, six aldermen across three wards and a city administrator. Rotary Park hosts the St. Charles County Fair and the St. Louis Renaissance Festival. The Wentzville R-IV School District covers Wentzville, Lake St. Louis, Foristell, Dardenne Prairie and part of O'Fallon, with four public high schools: Holt, Timberland, North Point and Liberty.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about homes in Wentzville?
sections.html:
Homes in Wentzville are mostly owned, and households are larger than in the inner-ring suburbs of St. Louis.

About 29.7 percent of residents are under 18, and the average household has 2.86 people. The mean commute of 27.8 minutes is longer than in University City, so a buyer will weigh the drive to St. Louis jobs.

sections.h2: What local details come up when buyers look at Wentzville?
sections.html:
Buyers often ask about schools, nearby colleges and community landmarks, and Wentzville has a few to mention in a listing. Lindenwood University runs a satellite campus in the former Southern Air Restaurant building, which was last owned by Chuck Berry. Midwest University and Urshan University also offer degrees in the city, and a branch of the St. Charles City-County Library serves residents.

The city is home to the first Vietnam Veterans Memorial in the United States. It began in 1967 as a tree of lights to raise money for gifts to servicemen, and by 1984 it had become a carved eagle atop a granite pillar. It is a regular stop on the national Run for the Wall trip. Private schools include St. Patrick School and Immanuel Lutheran School, both covering preschool through eighth grade.

None of these details change what a house is worth on their own, but a seller who can name the school district, the closest library and the commute to St. Louis gives buyers and investors a clearer picture of the address.

sections.h2: Does Wentzville require an inspection when I sell my house?
sections.html:
No. The City of Wentzville says no occupancy inspection is required when selling a house. The rule applies only if the house will be leased or rented, in which case an inspection must pass before a tenant moves in.

  • The residential occupancy inspection costs $50 and stays valid for 90 days.
  • It is requested through the city's SmartGov permit portal, and the city says it can usually be scheduled within one to two business days after payment.
  • The city requires a new inspection each time the resident changes at a property.
  • A new-construction buyer does not need one, because the builder obtains occupancy with the construction permit.

New service at the address also matters to a buyer: opening a water, trash and sewer account requires a $150 deposit, which the city holds until two years of good payment history and then credits to the account. The Building Division answers questions at (636) 327-5101, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: What are my choices for selling in Wentzville?
sections.html:
The usual routes are an agent listing, a sale by owner, or a sale to an investor. Because the city asks nothing of a seller for an owner-occupied sale, the difference between them comes down to time, cost and condition.

  • Agent listing. Ask for the commission rate in writing, plus an estimate of repair and staging costs.
  • Sale by owner. You manage pricing and showings yourself and still need a title company to close.
  • Investor offer. An investor may buy the house as it stands. If the investor plans to rent it, the $50 occupancy inspection becomes their task before a tenant moves in.

Look at what you owe first. A mortgage payoff, any home equity line and unpaid property tax come out of the proceeds at closing, so ask the title company for a payoff statement before you compare offers.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Wentzville house?
sections.html:
St. Charles County bills property tax for Wentzville. The Collector of Revenue's office is at 201 N. Second Street, Suite 134, in St. Charles, and its phone is 636-949-7470. The county accepts partial payments of at least $20 on a bill, although a partial payment does not keep a property out of the tax certificate sale.

  • Online or phone payments by e-check carry a $1.50 fee, and cards cost about 2.5 percent.
  • Mailed payments count on the USPS postmark date. A payment mailed on December 31 may not be postmarked until the next business day.
  • If you pay through your bank's bill-pay, start at least five working days before December 31, since the county counts the date it receives the payment.

To dispute a value, start with an informal hearing at the Assessor's Office, held from late April to early June, and call 636-949-7428 if you are outside a reassessment year. The next step is the Board of Equalization; the 2026 deadline was 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July, which has passed. After that comes the Missouri State Tax Commission, due September 30 or 30 days after the Board's decision, whichever is later. A property bought after the second Monday in June has until December 31. Full instructions are printed on the assessment notice you receive.

sections.h2: What should I do first if I want to sell my Wentzville house quickly?
sections.html:
Start by pulling together the numbers a buyer will ask about: the payoff on your loan, the latest county tax bill, any HOA dues and the last repairs you made. Then decide how much cleaning and fixing you will pay for before showing it.

If you want to avoid a long listing, ask investors for written offers and compare each one to a realistic listing price minus agent fees, repairs and carrying costs. Check who pays closing costs and what happens if the buyer backs out. If the house will be rented after the sale, remind the buyer about the city's $50 occupancy inspection and the 90-day validity window so the move-in date is not delayed.

faqs.q: Do I need a city inspection to sell my house in Wentzville?
faqs.a: No. Wentzville states that no occupancy inspection is required by the city when a house is sold. An inspection applies only when the house will be leased or rented to a new tenant.

faqs.q: How much is the Wentzville occupancy inspection?
faqs.a: It costs $50 and is valid for 90 days. It is requested through the SmartGov permit portal and is usually scheduled one to two business days after payment.

faqs.q: Which county collects property tax in Wentzville?
faqs.a: St. Charles County does. The Collector of Revenue is at 201 N. Second Street, Suite 134, in St. Charles, and can be reached at 636-949-7470.

faqs.q: Has the 2026 assessment appeal deadline passed in Wentzville?
faqs.a: Yes. The Board of Equalization form had to be received by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July 2026. A later appeal to the State Tax Commission requires a prior Board filing unless the property was newly purchased.

faqs.q: How large is Wentzville and how fast has it grown?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 49,495 residents for July 1, 2025, up from 44,372 in the 2020 count. The city covers roughly 20 square miles in western St. Charles County.
